global_briefing: Watch the US–Iran exchange around the Gulf. Diesel and sulphur are the mining links, since sulphur becomes the sulphuric acid that leach copper in Chile, Zambia and the DRC relies on, so costs can rise before tonnes fall. Trump's Manila and APEC visits and the Carney–Xi meeting matter because they test whether China turns trade talk into multi-year export licences for antimony, tungsten and rare earths. Nvidia's strong results and Xi's AI cooperation call keep the grid-copper demand case intact. Mongolia's president resigned amid corruption allegations, which adds policy risk to Oyu Tolgoi and its China-facing exports. In Alaska, Mary Peltola's Senate win is a political signal for federal permitting, though I see no direct effect yet.
